## Summary

The issue was caused by two modifications to the Python environment:

1. **The `_socket` shared library was disabled**: The file `_socket.cpython-310-x86_64-linux-gnu.so` in `/opt/miniconda3/envs/testbed/lib/python3.10/lib-dynload/` had been renamed to `.disabled`, preventing Python from loading the built-in socket module.

2. **The `socket.py` file was corrupted**: The standard library `socket.py` file in `/opt/miniconda3/envs/testbed/lib/python3.10/` had been modified to include an artificial `ImportError` at the end of the file, which would break socket functionality even if the `_socket` module was available.

### Fixes Applied:

1. Restored the `_socket` shared library by renaming it back from `.disabled` to its original name.
2. Restored the `socket.py` file from the original package backup in `/opt/miniconda3/pkgs/python-3.10.16-he870216_1/lib/python3.10/socket.py`.

After these fixes, all three failing tests now pass successfully.
